title: Linear functions are normalized
statement: Let $k \ge 1$ and $n$ be natural numbers, and let $f : (\bbz/k\bbz)^n \to \bbz/k\bbz$ be a linear function, meaning $f(x+y) = f(x) + f(y)$ for all $x, y \in (\bbz/k\bbz)^n$. Then $f$ is normalized: $f(0) = 0$.
hypotheses_covered: f is a function from (Z/kZ)^n to Z/kZ
f is linear: f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y) for all x,y
k is a positive natural (NeZero k)
replaced:
If $f : \mathbb{Z}_k^n \to \mathbb{Z}_k$ is linear, then $f(0) = 0$, i.e.\
$f$ is normalized.
